name: Xiufeng Li
affiliation: VIB Center for AI & Computational Biology
description: Xiufeng Li studies gene regulation, transposable elements and chromatin architecture, connecting mechanistic regulatory genomics with interpretable AI.
intro: I study how regulatory elements and chromatin architecture shape gene expression. My work brings together computational genomics and mechanistic biology to understand the regulatory logic of the genome.
about: I am a postdoctoral fellow at the VIB Center for AI & Computational Biology, working with Stein Aerts. I completed my PhD in Bioinformatics at Tsinghua University with Nian Liu, where I studied LINE-1-mediated gene activation and the regulation of hypertranscribed genes.
direction: I aim to connect mechanistic insights with interpretable AI to model how enhancers and gene loci integrate regulatory information across cell states.

research.title: Transposable elements as regulators
research.label: LINE-1 · long-range regulation
research.text: I investigated how LINE-1 transcription promotes chromatin contacts and activates distal genes, linking transposable elements to gene regulation and zygotic genome activation.

research.title: Safeguarding hypertranscribed genes
research.label: ANKRD11 · transcriptional control
research.text: I developed the hypertranscribed-gene analytical framework and integrated genomic datasets to study how ANKRD11 condensates restrain transcription at highly expressed developmental loci.

research.title: Interpretable models of gene regulation
research.label: Current direction
research.text: I aim to combine mechanistic regulatory genomics with interpretable AI to understand how distributed cis-regulatory information determines gene expression across cell states.

news.text: Joined the VIB Center for AI & Computational Biology as a postdoctoral fellow with Stein Aerts.
Our study of ANKRD11 condensates and hypertranscribed genes was published in Cell.
Our review of LINE-1 regulation and function was featured on the cover of Trends in Genetics.

publications.title: Condensates of the chromatin regulator ANKRD11 restrict hypertranscribed genes to safeguard development
publications.display_authors: Tao Zhang*, Xiufeng Li*, Wei Zhou, et al.
publications.summary: ANKRD11 condensates restrain hypertranscribed regions and safeguard transcriptional control during development.
publications.contribution: I co-conceived the study, led computational and integrative analyses, and developed the hypertranscribed-gene framework.

publications.title: Advances in understanding LINE-1 regulation and function in the human genome
publications.summary: A synthesis of LINE-1 regulation and its roles in genome organization, development and disease.
publications.contribution: I conceived and wrote the review, synthesized the literature, and developed its conceptual framework and figures.
publications.image_credit: Trends in Genetics · Volume 41, Issue 7 · July 2025 · Cell Press

publications.title: LINE-1 transcription activates long-range gene expression
publications.display_authors: Xiufeng Li*, Luyao Bie*, Yang Wang*, Yaqiang Hong*, et al.
publications.summary: Active LINE-1 elements promote long-range chromatin contacts and distal gene activation, including during zygotic genome activation.
publications.contribution: I led the computational and conceptual development, integrating genomic analyses into the mechanistic framework.

publications.title: SAFB restricts contact domain boundaries associated with L1 chimeric transcription
publications.display_authors: Yaqiang Hong*, Luyao Bie*, Tao Zhang*, et al., including Xiufeng Li
publications.summary: SAFB constrains chromatin contact-domain boundaries associated with L1 chimeric transcription.
